one_sentence: The sign operator σ with eigenvalues ±1 and commutation [σ, U]=0 maps moral orientation as binary and invariant under self-effort, requiring external grace for sign flip.
executive_summary: This document presents a structural isomorphism between a Hermitian sign operator σ in quantum mechanics (with eigenvalues ±1) and moral orientation in Christian theology (good/evil). The core claim is that self-generated unitary operations U cannot change the eigenvalue of σ when [σ, U]=0, mirroring the theological assertion that self-effort (works) cannot change moral status from fallen (−1) to righteous (+1). Key evidence includes the mathematical necessity of an external operator V with [σ, V]≠0 to flip the sign, paralleling grace as an external intervention. The conclusion is that Pelagianism is mathematically impossible under this mapping, while behavioral improvement within the −1 eigenspace is predicted and observable. The isomorphism is conditional on a binary view of moral status versus continuous behavior, with strong internal consistency within Reformed theology.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism record mapping a quantum sign operator to moral orientation in theology. The core claim is that self-generated operations cannot change the sign eigenvalue, paralleling the impossibility of self-salvation. Key evidence is the commutation relation [σ, U]=0, which forces sign invariance under internal dynamics, requiring an external operator for flip. This matters because it provides a precise mathematical framework for understanding grace versus works, with testable predictions and falsifiability conditions.
